items.followUp: State the main limitation of Dobereiner’s classification of elements.

rubric.why: Identifies the number of elements in a triad and their shared properties.
rubric.description: A triad consists of three elements with similar chemical properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both that there are three elements and that their properties are similar.

rubric.why: Gives the defining relationship between the atomic masses of the three elements.
rubric.description: The atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the middle element’s atomic mass is approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two.

modelAnswer: Dobereiner’s Triads are groups of three elements with similar chemical properties.
In each triad, the atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the arithmetic mean of the atomic masses of the other two elements.

items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds usually have high melting points?

rubric.why: Identifies the strong force holding the ions together.
rubric.description: Oppositely charged ions attract each other strongly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that strong electrostatic attraction acts between positive and negative ions.

rubric.why: Links the attractions between ions to the solid structure.
rubric.description: The ions are held in fixed positions in a crystal lattice, making the compound solid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the ions occupy fixed positions in a lattice or crystal structure.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds contain oppositely charged ions held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction.
The ions are held in fixed positions in a crystal lattice, so ionic compounds are solids.

items.followUp: Why do solid ionic compounds not conduct electricity, while their solutions do?

rubric.why: Identifies that ions can move in molten or dissolved ionic compounds.
rubric.description: In molten form or solution, the ions are free to move.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the ions become mobile or free to move.

rubric.why: Explains how mobile ions allow electric current to pass.
rubric.description: The moving ions carry electric charge through the molten compound or solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking mobile ions to carrying charge or conducting electricity.

modelAnswer: In solution or molten form, the ions in an ionic compound are free to move.
These mobile ions carry electric charge, so the solution or molten compound conducts electricity.

items.followUp: What kinds of solutes dissolve best in polar and nonpolar solvents?

rubric.why: States the matching rule for polar substances.
rubric.description: Polar solutes generally dissolve in polar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the polar-in-polar part of the principle.

rubric.why: States the matching rule for nonpolar substances.
rubric.description: Nonpolar solutes generally dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the nonpolar-in-nonpolar part of the principle.

modelAnswer: “Like dissolves like” means that polar solutes generally dissolve in polar solvents.
Similarly, nonpolar solutes generally dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
